messages:
alex: incident-bot just paged us for elevated SLO burn on text-gen-prod in us-west-2 — 5m burn spike at 2358012345. I’m looking at traces now.
incident-bot: ALERT: slo.burn_rate.text-gen-prod > 3.0 for 5m (multi-window). Pager sent to @eng-oncall. See: https://grafana/redwood/d/abc123
maria: oncall here, grabbing it. quick summary? customer impact?
jong: I'm seeing 502 surge from one frontend cluster to the model pool — request queueing causing request timeout cascades. Not a model OOM.
alex: confirmed, router logs show increased request latency -> 8s p50 to the pool. Likely a traffic surge from a partner test.
samira: tagging customer-success to check for reported incidents. @cs-team: any support tickets?
ops-bot: cs-ticket-3745 opened referencing slow responses from the API in the last 10m.
maria: mitigation plan: 1) temporary scale-up of ded pool, 2) adjust paging threshold to avoid noisy pages, 3) quick dashboard to monitor burn windows. I'll start scale-up.
jong: for paging threshold we should mute the 5m window alert and rely on the 1h window warm-up during the burst. Current rule:
```
alerts:
  - name: slo-burn-5m
    expr: burn_rate > 3.0
    window: 5m
    notify: pager
```
I propose: change notify for 5m -> slack-only, and keep pager on 1h window when it persists.
alex: agreed. 5m often noisy for short spikes. But we need an automated auto-silence that only triggers when burst is non-customer impacting.
maria: scaling now — requested +2 instances for dedicated pool, ETA 30s.
incident-bot: Scale request approved, ded-pool-redwood-42 scaling: +2 gpu nodes (started).
samira: CS reports 2 customers flagged degraded UX but no major errors, just timeouts on long requests. Not widespread.
jong: adding a temporary rule to ignore bursts caused by a single partner IP:
```
expr: burn_rate{partner_id!~"partner-prod-123"} > 3.0
```
But we should avoid hard-coding partner IDs in alerts. Maybe a suppression layer is better.
alex: +1 for suppression layer. We already have a 'burst-suppression' label in the router — can we feed that into alerting?
maria: yes, we can add `labels.include: burst_suppressed=true` to the 5m rule quickly. I'll push a config change to alertmanager.
ops-bot: alertmanager config change submitted by maria (PR #4321).
alex: while scaling completes, I'm going to enable prefix KV caching for the hot route to reduce load. Quick command: `rdctl cache enable --route text-gen-prod --ttl 60s`
jong: nice. That should reduce token compute churn.
incident-bot: ded-pool nodes ready (+2) at 2358012440.
maria: traffic is dropping back to baseline in the last minute, p50 latency down to 200ms. SLO burn window 5m still had a spike but 1h is safe.
samira: CS will send a note to the partner asking for a test postmortem; no escalations.
alex: follow-ups (post-incident): 1) Add a multi-window paging policy doc to the runbook that demotes 5m pages to slack-only unless accompanied by customer error spikes. 2) Add a dashboard tile that shows contributor IPs and partner_id distribution for quick triage. 3) Implement suppression labels upstream in router.
jong: also propose an adaptive budget policy that temporarily widens the multi-window tolerance during short, non-error bursts. E.g., require both burn_rate(5m) > 3 AND error_rate(5m) > 0.5% before paging.
maria: sounds good. I'll open tickets: ENG-812 (runbook update), ENG-813 (dashboard tile), ENG-814 (alert suppression pipeline).
alex: assign ENG-813 to jong for dashboard. ENG-814 to alex. ENG-812 to maria.
incident-bot: Incident resolved. All pages cleared at 2358012950. Duration ~10m.
samira: :thumbsup: low customer impact, good coordination.
jong: leaving a note in the postmortem: avoid muting 5m alerts blindly — prefer soft-action (slack notify) + automated suppression matching router labels.
maria: will draft a short post-incident note and link the PR that edited alertmanager.
alex: thanks all — nice quick mitigation. Follow-up sync tomorrow 10:00 to review multi-window tuning and SLA budget implications.
